_comment: Curated metadata for selected Nintendo Entertainment System entries. Entries not listed here still appear in the library using their filename-derived title and the platform's generic guidance.

nes/Super Mario Bros.nes.title: Super Mario Bros.
nes/Super Mario Bros.nes.desc: Mario runs through the Mushroom Kingdom to rescue Princess Peach, defining the side-scrolling platformer along the way.
nes/Super Mario Bros.nes.history: Designed by Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka, Super Mario Bros. helped revive the North American console market after the 1983 crash.

nes/Super_mario_brothers.nes.title: Super Mario Bros.
nes/Super_mario_brothers.nes.desc: An alternate filename of Super Mario Bros. present in the collection, using a different naming convention.

nes/Super Mario Bros. 3.nes.title: Super Mario Bros. 3
nes/Super Mario Bros. 3.nes.desc: Mario travels eight kingdoms with a world map, suits that grant flight and a frog form, and Koopalings as bosses.
nes/Super Mario Bros. 3.nes.history: Widely regarded as the definitive NES platformer, Super Mario Bros. 3 sold enormously and was later bundled with the NES in North America.

nes/Smb3.nes.title: Super Mario Bros. 3
nes/Smb3.nes.desc: A short-filename copy of Super Mario Bros. 3 held in the collection.

nes/Super_mario_brothers3.nes.title: Super Mario Bros. 3
nes/Super_mario_brothers3.nes.desc: Another filename variant of Super Mario Bros. 3 present in the collection.

nes/Super_mario_brothers2.nes.title: Super Mario Bros. 2
nes/Super_mario_brothers2.nes.desc: The Western Super Mario Bros. 2, a reworked Doki Doki Panic with four playable characters and a dream-world setting.

nes/Zelda.nes.title: The Legend of Zelda
nes/Zelda.nes.desc: An open-world adventure in which Link explores Hyrule, collects fragments of the Triforce and rescues Zelda from Ganon.
nes/Zelda.nes.history: The first console game with a battery-backed save, The Legend of Zelda established the action-adventure genre.

nes/Zelda2.nes.title: Zelda II: The Adventure of Link
nes/Zelda2.nes.desc: A side-scrolling sequel with experience points, towns and palaces, departing sharply from the first game's top-down design.

nes/Metroid.nes.title: Metroid
nes/Metroid.nes.desc: Samus Aran explores the labyrinth of Zebes, finding power-ups that unlock new areas and fighting Mother Brain.
nes/Metroid.nes.history: Metroid introduced the non-linear exploration structure later named after the series, and its ending revealed Samus as a woman.

nes/Castlevania.nes.title: Castlevania
nes/Castlevania.nes.desc: Simon Belmont whips his way through Dracula's castle, with stair-climbing, sub-weapons and a famous clock tower.

nes/Castlevania2.nes.title: Castlevania II: Simon's Quest
nes/Castlevania2.nes.desc: A non-linear sequel with day/night cycles, towns and a cryptic quest to lift Dracula's curse.

nes/castlevania3.nes.title: Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse
nes/castlevania3.nes.desc: Trevor Belmont travels with three possible companions, choosing branching routes through Wallachia to reach Dracula.

nes/Contra.nes.title: Contra
nes/Contra.nes.desc: A run-and-gun shooter with two-player co-op, spread guns and a famous 30-lives code.
nes/Contra.nes.history: Contra was adapted into the NES launch-period hit with an added overhead stage, and its code (up, up, down, down...) became one of gaming's best-known secrets.

nes/Super_c.nes.title: Super C
nes/Super_c.nes.desc: The NES sequel to Contra, replacing the arcade port's stages with original levels and a top-down base assault.

nes/Megaman.nes.title: Mega Man
nes/Megaman.nes.desc: Mega Man picks a stage order freely and earns each Robot Master's weapon, defining the series' core structure.

nes/Megaman2.nes.title: Mega Man 2
nes/Megaman2.nes.desc: A refined sequel with eight Robot Masters, Energy Tanks and a celebrated soundtrack.

nes/Megaman3.nes.title: Mega Man 3
nes/Megaman3.nes.desc: Adds the slide, Rush and Proto Man, doubling the Robot Master count with a second set of Doc Robots.

nes/Megaman 4.nes.title: Mega Man 4
nes/Megaman 4.nes.desc: Introduces the charged Mega Buster and a new antagonist, Dr. Cossack.

nes/Megaman 5.nes.title: Mega Man 5
nes/Megaman 5.nes.desc: Features Beat the robot bird and a plot centred on Proto Man's apparent betrayal.

nes/Megaman 6.nes.title: Mega Man 6
nes/Megaman 6.nes.desc: The final NES Mega Man, adding the Jet and Power adapters and a global tournament storyline.

nes/Ninja_gaiden.nes.title: Ninja Gaiden
nes/Ninja_gaiden.nes.desc: Ryu Hayabusa fights through cinematic side-scrolling stages with wall jumps, a windmill shuriken and animated cutscenes.

nes/Ninja_gaiden2.nes.title: Ninja Gaiden II: The Dark Sword of Chaos
nes/Ninja_gaiden2.nes.desc: A sequel adding clone shadows, more vertical level design and a longer story.

nes/Ninja_gaiden3.nes.title: Ninja Gaiden III: The Ancient Ship of Doom
nes/Ninja_gaiden3.nes.desc: The final NES Ninja Gaiden, with a limited continue system and a more punishing difficulty curve.

nes/final_fantasy.nes.title: Final Fantasy
nes/final_fantasy.nes.desc: Four Light Warriors restore the crystals in the RPG that established the series, with a job class system and airship travel.

nes/Dragon_warrior.nes.title: Dragon Warrior
nes/Dragon_warrior.nes.desc: The North American release of Dragon Quest, a turn-based RPG in which the hero saves a kingdom from the Dragonlord.

nes/Dragon_warrior2.nes.title: Dragon Warrior II
nes/Dragon_warrior2.nes.desc: A larger world with a party of three and a ship, expanding the original's structure.

nes/Dragon_warrior3.nes.title: Dragon Warrior III
nes/Dragon_warrior3.nes.desc: Introduces a class-changing party system and a world that connects back to the first game.

nes/Dragon_warrior4.nes.title: Dragon Warrior IV
nes/Dragon_warrior4.nes.desc: Tells its story in chapters following separate characters before uniting them in a final chapter.

nes/Duck_hunt.nes.title: Duck Hunt
nes/Duck_hunt.nes.desc: A light-gun shooting game in which the player shoots ducks and clay pigeons, with the laughing dog as its mascot.

nes/Punch Out.nes.title: Punch-Out!!
nes/Punch Out.nes.desc: Little Mac climbs the boxing ranks, learning each opponent's tells across a memorable cast of fighters.

nes/Mike_tyson\u0027s_punch_out.nes.title: Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!!
nes/Mike_tyson\u0027s_punch_out.nes.desc: The original release of Punch-Out!! featuring Mike Tyson as the final opponent, later replaced by Mr. Dream.

nes/Tetris.nes.title: Tetris
nes/Tetris.nes.desc: The NES version of Tetris, with the flat 'Type A' mode and the rising-garbage 'Type B' mode.

nes/Kirby\u0027s_adventure.nes.title: Kirby's Adventure
nes/Kirby\u0027s_adventure.nes.desc: Kirby inhales enemies to gain copy abilities across Dream Land, in one of the NES's most technically impressive late titles.

nes/Kid_icarus.nes.title: Kid Icarus
nes/Kid_icarus.nes.desc: Pit climbs from the underworld to Skyworld, mixing vertical platforming with shops and dungeons.

nes/Excite_bike.nes.title: Excitebike
nes/Excite_bike.nes.desc: A motocross time trial with a track editor and a temperature gauge that punishes over-revving.

nes/Ice_climber.nes.title: Ice Climber
nes/Ice_climber.nes.desc: Popo and Nana climb icy mountains, breaking blocks and dodging topis and polar bears in two-player play.

nes/Bubble_bobble.nes.title: Bubble Bobble
nes/Bubble_bobble.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Taito's bubble-trapping platformer, with two-player co-op and a hundred stages.

nes/Bubble_bobble2.nes.title: Bubble Bobble Part 2
nes/Bubble_bobble2.nes.desc: A sequel with new enemies, larger levels and a different progression structure.

nes/Gradius.nes.title: Gradius
nes/Gradius.nes.desc: A horizontal shooter built around a power-up bar that upgrades speed, missiles, lasers and options.

nes/Life_force.nes.title: Life Force
nes/Life_force.nes.desc: A Gradius spin-off set inside a living alien, with two-player co-op and organic stage design.

nes/Metal Gear.nes.title: Metal Gear
nes/Metal Gear.nes.desc: Solid Snake infiltrates Outer Heaven, avoiding detection and gathering items in an early stealth-action game.

nes/Crystalis.nes.title: Crystalis
nes/Crystalis.nes.desc: A post-apocalyptic action RPG with real-time sword combat, elemental weapons and a large overworld.

nes/Faxanadu.nes.title: Faxanadu
nes/Faxanadu.nes.desc: A side-scrolling action RPG in which a wanderer restores a dying world tree, using shops, mantras and equipment.

nes/river_city_ransom.nes.title: River City Ransom
nes/river_city_ransom.nes.desc: A beat-'em-up with RPG elements, shops and free roaming across River City.

nes/Double_dragon.nes.title: Double Dragon
nes/Double_dragon.nes.desc: The NES adaptation of the arcade brawler, adding a two-player mode and a level-up system for moves.

nes/Double_dragon2.nes.title: Double Dragon II: The Revenge
nes/Double_dragon2.nes.desc: A sequel with directional attacks, platforming sections and two-player co-op.

nes/Double_dragon3.nes.title: Double Dragon III: The Sacred Stones
nes/Double_dragon3.nes.desc: The third NES Double Dragon, with multiple playable characters and limited continues.

nes/Battle_toads.nes.title: Battletoads
nes/Battle_toads.nes.desc: A notoriously difficult brawler with vehicle stages, including the speeder bike level.

nes/Duck_tales.nes.title: DuckTales
nes/Duck_tales.nes.desc: Scrooge McDuck pogo-jumps through five stages in any order, searching for treasures and the moon's hidden level.

nes/Bionic_commando.nes.title: Bionic Commando
nes/Bionic_commando.nes.desc: A grappling-hook action game in which Ladd Spencer swings across military installations without a jump button.

nes/Blaster_master.nes.title: Blaster Master
nes/Blaster_master.nes.desc: A vehicle-and-on-foot adventure in which Jason explores a subterranean world in the SOPHIA tank.

nes/Batman.nes.title: Batman: The Video Game
nes/Batman.nes.desc: A stylish platformer based on the 1989 film, with wall jumps and a memorable Sunsoft soundtrack.

nes/Marble_madness.nes.title: Marble Madness
nes/Marble_madness.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Atari's isometric marble race, controlled with the D-pad.

nes/Rampage.nes.title: Rampage
nes/Rampage.nes.desc: The NES version of the monster-smashing arcade game, with three selectable creatures.

nes/Kung_fu.nes.title: Kung Fu
nes/Kung_fu.nes.desc: A vertically scrolling beat-'em-up in which Thomas rescues Sylvia from five floors of martial artists.

nes/Popeye.nes.title: Popeye
nes/Popeye.nes.desc: The NES port of Nintendo's arcade game, with Popeye collecting hearts and spinach while avoiding Bluto.

nes/Donkey Kong.nes.title: Donkey Kong
nes/Donkey Kong.nes.desc: The NES conversion of the arcade original, retaining the first three screens.

nes/Donkey_kong_jr.nes.title: Donkey Kong Jr.
nes/Donkey_kong_jr.nes.desc: The NES port of Donkey Kong Jr., in which the young ape climbs vines to free his father.

nes/Donkey_kong3.nes.title: Donkey Kong 3
nes/Donkey_kong3.nes.desc: The NES port of the greenhouse shooter starring Stanley the exterminator.

nes/Donkey Kong Classics.nes.title: Donkey Kong Classics
nes/Donkey Kong Classics.nes.desc: A cartridge compiling Donkey Kong and Donkey Kong Jr. on a single NES game pack.

nes/Mario_brothers.nes.title: Mario Bros.
nes/Mario_brothers.nes.desc: The NES port of the arcade game in which Mario and Luigi bump enemies from below and kick them away.

nes/Galaga.nes.title: Galaga
nes/Galaga.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Namco's formation shooter, with the capture-and-rescue mechanic intact.

nes/Pacman.nes.title: Pac-Man
nes/Pacman.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Pac-Man, released on the Famicom in 1984 and later in North America.

nes/Ms_pacman.nes.title: Ms. Pac-Man
nes/Ms_pacman.nes.desc: The NES version of Ms. Pac-Man, released late in the console's life as a Tengen/Namco title.

nes/Ms. Pacman.nes.title: Ms. Pac-Man
nes/Ms. Pacman.nes.desc: An alternate filename of the NES Ms. Pac-Man present in the collection.

nes/Q Bert.nes.title: Q*bert
nes/Q Bert.nes.desc: The NES conversion of the isometric pyramid puzzler.

nes/Digdug.nes.title: Dig Dug II
nes/Digdug.nes.desc: The NES release of Dig Dug II, in which fault lines are drilled to sink island sections.

nes/Joust.nes.title: Joust
nes/Joust.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Williams' ostrich-knight arcade game.

nes/Millipede.nes.title: Millipede
nes/Millipede.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Atari's bug shooter, with the original's mushroom field and new enemies.

nes/Arkanoid.nes.title: Arkanoid
nes/Arkanoid.nes.desc: The NES conversion of the brick-breaking arcade game, with power-up capsules and boss stages.

nes/Spy_hunter.nes.title: Spy Hunter
nes/Spy_hunter.nes.desc: The NES conversion of the spy-car arcade game, with weapons van upgrades.

nes/Toobin.nes.title: Toobin'
nes/Toobin.nes.desc: The NES conversion of the river-rafting arcade game.

nes/Klax.nes.title: Klax
nes/Klax.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Atari's tile-matching puzzler.

nes/Tecmo Bowl.nes.title: Tecmo Bowl
nes/Tecmo Bowl.nes.desc: A fast American football game with a simplified playbook and a much-loved two-player mode.

nes/Tspr Bowl.nes.title: Tecmo Super Bowl
nes/Tspr Bowl.nes.desc: An expanded Tecmo Bowl with full NFL teams, a season mode and stat tracking.

nes/Rbi Baseball.nes.title: R.B.I. Baseball
nes/Rbi Baseball.nes.desc: A fast, arcade-style baseball game with real MLB players and a simple one-button swing.

nes/Ghost_\u0026_goblins.nes.title: Ghosts'n Goblins
nes/Ghost_\u0026_goblins.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Arthur's graveyard quest, retaining the arcade's unforgiving difficulty.

nes/Gargoyle\u0027s_quest2.nes.title: Gargoyle's Quest II
nes/Gargoyle\u0027s_quest2.nes.desc: A Firebrand adventure mixing overworld exploration, action stages and RPG-style progression.

nes/Startropics.nes.title: StarTropics
nes/Startropics.nes.desc: A top-down adventure in which Mike Jones searches tropical islands for his uncle, using a yo-yo and a submarine.

nes/Maniac_mansion.nes.title: Maniac Mansion
nes/Maniac_mansion.nes.desc: A point-and-click adventure with multiple characters and several possible endings, ported to the NES with changes.

nes/Shadowgate.nes.title: Shadowgate
nes/Shadowgate.nes.desc: A first-person point-and-click adventure in which the player explores a castle and must avoid fatal mistakes.

nes/Deja_vu.nes.title: Déjà Vu
nes/Deja_vu.nes.desc: A noir point-and-click mystery in which the player wakes with amnesia and must clear their name.

nes/Uninvited.nes.title: Uninvited
nes/Uninvited.nes.desc: A horror point-and-click adventure set in a haunted mansion, with a driving sequence and multiple endings.

nes/Wizards_n_warriors.nes.title: Wizards & Warriors
nes/Wizards_n_warriors.nes.desc: Kuros the knight searches castles for gems and rescues princesses, with vertical exploration and hidden items.

nes/Little_nemo.nes.title: Little Nemo: The Dream Master
nes/Little_nemo.nes.desc: Nemo explores dream worlds, feeding candy to animals and wearing them to gain their abilities.

nes/Yoshi.nes.title: Yoshi
nes/Yoshi.nes.desc: A falling-block puzzle game in which Mario stacks egg halves to hatch Yoshi.

nes/Wario\u0027s_world.nes.title: Wario's Woods
nes/Wario\u0027s_world.nes.desc: Toad clears monsters by matching colours in a puzzle game with a story mode and a two-player battle.

nes/Adventure Island 2.nes.title: Adventure Island II
nes/Adventure Island 2.nes.desc: Master Higgins explores eight islands with dinosaur companions, skateboards and hidden eggs.

nes/Adventure Island 3.nes.title: Adventure Island 3
nes/Adventure Island 3.nes.desc: A further Adventure Island sequel with new dinosaur helpers and a world map.

nes/Adventures of Lolo.nes.title: Adventures of Lolo
nes/Adventures of Lolo.nes.desc: A block-pushing puzzle game in which Lolo rescues Lala across single-screen chambers.

nes/Bomber_man.nes.title: Bomberman
nes/Bomber_man.nes.desc: The NES Bomberman, with maze stages, bomb upgrades and a battle mode.

nes/Bomber_man2.nes.title: Bomberman II
nes/Bomber_man2.nes.desc: A sequel with a story mode, new items and three-player battle support.

nes/Snow_brothers.nes.title: Snow Bros.
nes/Snow_brothers.nes.desc: Two snowmen trap enemies in snowballs and roll them into each other across single-screen stages.

nes/Paperboy.nes.title: Paperboy
nes/Paperboy.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Atari's paper round, with a scrolling street and subscriber list.

nes/Alien_syndrome.nes.title: Alien Syndrome
nes/Alien_syndrome.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Sega's top-down alien shooter, with hostage rescue and a timer.

nes/1942.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Capcom's vertical WWII shooter.

nes/1943.nes.title: 1943: The Battle of Midway
nes/1943.nes.desc: The NES conversion of 1943, with an energy bar and a shop-style upgrade system.

nes/Commando.nes.title: Commando
nes/Commando.nes.desc: A vertical run-and-gun in which a soldier advances through enemy lines with grenades and a machine gun.

nes/Jackal.nes.title: Jackal
nes/Jackal.nes.desc: A top-down jeep shooter with hostage rescue and grenade upgrades.

nes/Section_z.nes.title: Section Z
nes/Section_z.nes.desc: A side-scrolling shooter with a non-linear station map and two-directional fire.

nes/Rush_n_attack.nes.title: Rush'n Attack
nes/Rush_n_attack.nes.desc: A side-scrolling combat game in which a soldier fights through enemy bases with a knife and collected weapons.

nes/Ikari_warriors.nes.title: Ikari Warriors
nes/Ikari_warriors.nes.desc: A vertical run-and-gun with rotating movement and a two-player co-op mode.

nes/Cobra_command.nes.title: Cobra Command
nes/Cobra_command.nes.desc: A helicopter shooter with side-scrolling and top-down stages, ported from the arcade laserdisc game.

nes/Top_gun.nes.title: Top Gun
nes/Top_gun.nes.desc: A flight combat game based on the film, with carrier landings and missile combat.

nes/Operation_wolf.nes.title: Operation Wolf
nes/Operation_wolf.nes.desc: The NES conversion of Taito's light-gun hostage-rescue shooter, played with the controller or Zapper.

nes/Batman_returns.nes.title: Batman Returns
nes/Batman_returns.nes.desc: A side-scrolling brawler based on the film, with Batman fighting through Gotham.
